gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
'You should get a second opinion,' the doctor said. The doctor ___ a second opinion.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the reporting verb that takes object + to-infinitive; suggest and offer do not.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't touch the wet paint,' the caretaker warned us. The caretaker warned us ___ the wet paint.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands become not to + infinitive after told/asked/warned.

gaps.sentence: "Can you help me?" — She asked ___ help her.
'I'll pay for the damage,' he said. He ___ pay for the damage.
gaps.explanation: 'I'll pay' as a voluntary act is reported with 'offered to pay'.

gaps.sentence: 'We might have missed the turning,' he admitted. He admitted that they ___ have missed the turning.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form, so it is unchanged.

gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.

gaps.sentence: 'It was your team that missed the deadline,' the director told us. The director ___ missing the deadline.
gaps.explanation: 'Blame somebody for something' is the correct pattern; 'accuse' takes 'of'.
